summary: Formal community response remains limited because the project is pre-application and no application is open for representations. Apatura held statutory pre-application consultation in September 2025, including a public exhibition at Allan Glens Rugby Club, Bishopbriggs, on 29 September and an online consultation site. Organised local opposition is now represented by NO data centres in East Dunbartonshire, a signatory to the August 2026 community-campaign coalition letter. APRS tracks the site in its national data-centres campaign, characterising it as Green Belt farmland between Bishopbriggs and Lenzie and calling for a moratorium; Foxglove included it in its December 2025 analysis of the aggregate electricity demand of planned Scottish data centres. No community-council position, objection count or East Dunbartonshire Council member statement was located.

principal_concerns.concern: Loss of Green Belt farmland between Bishopbriggs and Lenzie
principal_concerns.developer_response: Apatura states the site is partially Green Belt but allocated for development within the adopted Westerhill Regeneration Area, with landscaping/screening and ecological mitigation zones proposed.

principal_concerns.concern: Aggregate electricity demand of planned Scottish data centres (Westerhill counted at 300MW within a 2,000-3,000MW national pipeline)

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: Community benefit fund coordinated by the council through Section 75 agreements, potentially administered with a partner such as Foundation Scotland
Potential recovered-heat supply to local district heating networks via an on-site heat-exchange plant
Skills partnerships with local colleges and universities; jobs and investment supporting the Westerhill Regeneration Area vision

stakeholder_positions.position: Monitors the proposal within its data centres campaign; nationally seeks a moratorium on hyperscale AI data centres until governance and policy frameworks are, in its view, fit for purpose.

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: NO data centres in East Dunbartonshire
stakeholder_positions.position: Opposed; signed the community-campaign coalition letter seeking a moratorium on hyperscale AI data-centre decisions pending national safeguards.

campaign_groups: NO data centres in East Dunbartonshire
planning_authority_contact: East Dunbartonshire Council, 12 Strathkelvin Place, Kirkintilloch G66 1TJ; 0300 123 4510; customerservices@eastdunbarton.gov.uk
notes: Objection/support counts will only exist once a full application is validated. The council's position as planning authority is undetermined; note the council separately promotes the Westerhill Regeneration Area masterplan within which the site sits, which may be a point of local debate about its dual role.
